explanation: Falafel in the Levant is usually made with chickpeas, but Egyptian cooks grind soaked dried fava beans with plenty of fresh herbs, which turn the inside green.

claims.text: Egyptian falafel (ta'ameya) is made mainly from dried fava beans, also called broad beans.
Ta'ameya is not made mainly from chickpeas, red lentils or mung beans.
Falafel in the Levant is usually made with chickpeas.
Ta'ameya is made from soaked, ground dried fava beans mixed with fresh herbs, which make the inside green.
